newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk to transfer some costs to local authority.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk to transfer some costs to local authority.

text.p: The financially troubled flagship plant of Russia's Norilsk Nickel has reached a preliminary deal for regional authorities to bear the cost of supporting some infrastructure where the plant is based.
A Norilsk press release said on Monday that the company would transfer some housing and other buildings to the Arctic town of Norilsk, relieving the plant of maintenance costs.
Parent company RAO Norilsky Nickel has said the burden of shouldering the cost of all property and services in the town is hurting cash flows and is partly responsible for wage arrears.

Workers at the main Norilsk plant, the mining and metallurgical combine, have threatened to disrupt output on March 27 -- a day of national protest called by trade unions and opposition leaders -- and again from April 2 over salary and holiday arrears and related issues.
The Norilsk group is a major world producer of nickel, platinum group metals and other metals.
